questions.stem: Justify the asymptotic behavior of the following curves using the language of limits.
questions.hint: Write a full structured solution for the teacher to mark.

steps.explain: Evaluate the limits as \( x \to \pm\infty \) or \( x \to 0 \).

questions.stem: Some curves can cross their asymptotes. Consider the curve \( y = \frac{4x}{x^2+1} \).
questions.hint: Write a full structured solution for the teacher to mark.

steps.explain: As \( x \to \pm\infty \), the denominator \( x^2+1 \) grows much faster than \( 4x \), so \( y \to 0 \). Thus \( y = 0 \) (the x-axis) is the horizontal asymptote.
Find where \( y = 0 \) (crosses asymptote): \( \frac{4x}{x^2+1} = 0 \implies 4x = 0 \implies x = 0 \). The crossing point is \( (0, 0) \).
